subject: ss-haematology
title: Iron deficiency anaemia of inflammation and iron overload
refs: Harrison Principles of Internal Medicine 22e Ch 102 Iron Deficiency and Other Acquired Anemias
World Health Organization guideline on iron deficiency 2024

steps.tx: Iron is conserved and reused, with only **1** to **2** mg absorbed daily against equal losses, while macrophage recycling supplies **20** to **25** mg. **Transferrin** (iron carrying protein) is the central carrier. **Ferritin** (storage protein) below **30** micrograms per litre diagnoses absolute iron deficiency with **92** percent sensitivity and **98** percent specificity, and absent marrow iron remains the gold standard.
steps.say: Daily absorption is only one to two milligrams, dwarfed by macrophage recycled iron. Ferritin below thirty confirms absolute deficiency. Marrow iron absence is the gold standard but is rarely needed.

steps.tx: **Hepcidin** (liver peptide locking iron in stores) and **ferroportin** (iron export pump) govern the whole system. Iron lack lowers hepcidin and opens ferroportin, while inflammation raises hepcidin and sequesters iron in macrophages. **TMPRSS6** mutations cause **IRIDA** (iron refractory iron deficiency anaemia), a rare condition deaf to oral iron. **DCYTB** (duodenal iron reducer) and **DMT1** (duodenal iron importer) handle uptake.
steps.say: Hepcidin locks iron away by closing ferroportin, while iron lack opens it again. IRIDA is a rare genetic cause of oral iron failure. Inflammation produces functional deficiency through high hepcidin.

steps.tx: Iron deficiency affects about **1.2** billion people, nearly half the anaemic population. Growth, heavy menses, pregnancy and **blood loss** (especially gut) drive it, and multiple causes often coexist. Early deficiency leaves MCV normal while ferritin falls first. **Pica** (craving ice or soil), **koilonychia** (spoon nails), glossitis and **Plummer Vinson syndrome** (dysphagia from oesophageal webs) clinch the clinical picture.
steps.say: Iron deficiency touches over a billion people worldwide. Ferritin falls before MCV does, so early deficiency can hide. Pica and spoon nails are classic bedside clues.

steps.tx: The iron panel pattern separates the mimics. Iron deficiency shows low ferritin, low transferrin saturation and high **sTfR** (soluble transferrin receptor), while **anaemia of inflammation** (anaemia of chronic disease) shows normal to high ferritin with low saturation. Mixed states show ferritin below **70** to **100**. Thalassaemia trait keeps ferritin and saturation normal despite microcytosis, a key exam trap.
steps.say: Ferritin and transferrin saturation separate iron deficiency from inflammation. Thalassaemia trait keeps both normal despite small cells. Mixed states sit in the middle range of ferritin.

steps.tx: Inflammation drives anaemia through interleukin **6** (IL-6, inflammatory cytokine) raising hepcidin, while **TNF** (tumour necrosis factor) and **interferon gamma** suppress **erythropoietin** (EPO, kidney hormone) response. **CKD** (chronic kidney disease) anaemia appears once more than **50** percent of kidney function is lost and carries cardiac risk. Heart failure also shows iron deficiency in **50** to **60** percent, and intravenous iron improves symptoms there.
steps.say: Interleukin six raises hepcidin and locks iron away in inflammation. Kidney disease anaemia worsens as function falls below half. Heart failure iron deficiency responds to intravenous iron.

steps.tx: Oral ferrous salts supply **65** to **100** mg elemental iron daily or alternate day, and treatment continues months after haemoglobin normalises to refill stores. **Intravenous iron** (iron sucrose, ferric carboxymaltose up to **1000** mg) suits malabsorption, inflammation and heart failure with ferritin below **100** or saturation below **20** percent. In dialysis care, targets aim for saturation **30** to **40** percent with ferritin **200** to **700**.
steps.say: Oral iron is given daily or alternate day and continued after haemoglobin recovers. Intravenous iron suits malabsorption and heart failure. Saturation and ferritin targets guide dialysis care.

steps.tx: **Iron overload** (excess body iron) injures liver, heart and pancreas. Ferritin above **1000** with transferrin saturation high flags overload, and **MRI T2** (magnetic resonance T2 mapping) quantifies liver and cardiac iron better than ferritin. **Phlebotomy** (regular therapeutic bleeding) is first line in haemochromatosis, while **deferasirox** (oral chelator) and deferoxamine clear transfusional iron. Hypophosphataemia now limits several intravenous iron salts.
steps.say: Iron overload damages liver, heart and pancreas over time. MRI T2 quantifies tissue iron better than ferritin. Phlebotomy clears genetic overload while chelators handle transfusional iron.

steps.tx: Every man and postmenopausal woman with iron deficiency needs upper and lower gut evaluation to exclude cancer, especially right colon malignancy. Hookworm, heavy menses and **von Willebrand disease** (clotting factor lack) interact frequently. **Heyde syndrome** (aortic stenosis, bleeding and acquired von Willebrand deficiency) links iron loss to valve disease. Missing endoscopy in older men is an indefensible exam error.
steps.say: Men and postmenopausal women need gut evaluation to exclude cancer. Von Willebrand disease often hides behind heavy menses. Heyde syndrome ties aortic stenosis to iron losing bleeding.

steps.tx: **Prolyl hydroxylase inhibitors** (oral HIF stabilisers) raise both EPO and gut iron absorption and are approved in some countries for kidney disease anaemia, though long term safety remains uncertain. **ESAs** (erythropoiesis stimulating agents) stay standard in kidney care with a haemoglobin target below **11.5** grams per decilitre driven by iron coadministration. Restrictive transfusion thresholds of **7** to **8** grams per decilitre now govern stable intensive care patients.
steps.say: Prolyl hydroxylase inhibitors raise both EPO and iron absorption. ESA therapy stays the kidney disease standard with iron support. Stable intensive care patients get restrictive transfusion thresholds.

steps.tx: High yield anchors: ferritin below **30** equals absolute deficiency; saturation below **15** to **20** percent restricts erythropoiesis; thalassaemia trait keeps ferritin normal; **IRIDA** resists oral iron; IV iron is indicated in heart failure under defined cutoffs; phlebotomy treats genetic overload; and MRI T2 beats ferritin for tissue iron. B12 and folate must be checked in malabsorption before calling iron therapy a failure.
steps.say: Ferritin below thirty means absolute deficiency, and normal ferritin never excludes thalassaemia trait confusion. IRIDA resists oral iron alone. MRI T2 remains the best tissue iron measure.
